items.statement: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space, including dimension zero. Let V:E→ℝ be C². Let α,β≥0 and η∈ℝ satisfy α>0, α≤β, α‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤β‖v‖² for every x,v∈E, η>0 and βη≤1. Fix arbitrary y,r∈E and z=(x,p)∈E×E. Define c=y−η∇V(r), Φ_s(z)=(c+cos(s)(x−c)+√η sin(s)p, −sin(s)(x−c)/√η+cos(s)p), g_r(x)=∇V(x)−∇V(r), S_r(x,p)=(x,p−2〈p,g_r(x)〉g_r(x)/‖g_r(x)‖²), and λ_r(x,p)=√η max{0,〈p,g_r(x)〉}. Total real division makes S_r the identity when g_r(x)=0. For t≥0 set Λ_z(t)=∫₀ᵗλ_r(Φ_s(z))ds and τ_z(e)=inf{t≥0:Λ_z(t)≥e}∈[0,∞], with inf empty=∞. Let Ω=ℝ^ℕ, P=⊗_(k≥0)Exp(1), ε_k(sample)=max{sample_k,0}, and U(sample)=τ_z(ε_0(sample)). Thus the authors first threshold is canonical coordinate0, not a supplied clock or law. Set F(sample)=untopD_0(U(sample)), viewed as a real number; it is the finite waiting time when U is finite and zero at infinity. For every finite T≥0 define A_T={sample:0<U(sample)≤T}, d_z(s)=λ_r(Φ_s(z))exp(−Λ_z(max{s,0})), ρ_T=(Lebesgue restricted to (0,T]).withDensity(ofReal(d_z)), and J_z(s)=(max{s,0},S_r(Φ_s(z)))∈[0,∞)×(E×E), for all real s. Then U,F,J_z are Borel measurable. For every finite T, A_T is measurable, F_*(P restricted to A_T)=ρ_T, and (J_z∘F)_*(P restricted to A_T)=(J_z)_*ρ_T. Moreover ρ_T is a finite subprobability measure, ρ_T(ℝ)=1−exp(−Λ_z(T))≤1. For every Borel real h on [0,∞)×(E×E), every M≥0 with |h(a)|≤M for all a, h∈L¹((J_z)_*ρ_T), h∘J_z∘F∈L¹(P restricted to A_T), and s↦h(J_z(s))d_z(s)∈L¹(Lebesgue restricted to (0,T]); their exact integral identity is ∫_(A_T)h(J_z(F(sample)))P(dsample)=∫₀ᵀh(s,S_r(Φ_s(z)))λ_r(Φ_s(z))exp(−Λ_z(s))ds, with the right-hand side understood over (0,T]. All assertions hold for every y,r,z,T, with E,V,α,β,η fixed. Infinity is excluded by A_T before the default finite projection is used; zero thresholds and zero waiting times are excluded by its positive guard and have zero P-mass by the derived survival law at0. The finite-event mass is not renormalized; the missing mass is exp(−Λ_z(T)) and includes waits beyond T and infinite waits. No strict hazard increase, positive rate, almost-sure finite wait, uniform cap, supplied measurability, density or integrability assumption is added. T=0, M=0, rank0, zero normals and flat hazards are included. This is an attributed ASTIS measure-theoretic completion of the actual first-event density factor implicit in the authors AppendixA.1(A.1),(A.2),(A.7), using their actual dynamics and iid clocks. It does not prove the successive conditional factors, full finite-event path expansion, path reversal, invariance, process Markovness, all-L² contraction, mixing, implemented error/cost, actual-input composition or complete main results.
assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space, including dimension zero. V:E→ℝ is real-valued and C².
The six original analytic hypotheses are α>0; α≤β; V∈C²; α‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤β‖v‖² for every x,v; η>0; βη≤1. α,β are nonnegative. No higher derivative bound is assumed.

Standing E,V,α,β,η are fixed. Every deterministic y,r,z and finite T≥0 is allowed. P is the canonical countable product of real rate-one exponential measures; U uses ε_0. All fourteen P,ε,c,Φ,S,λ,Λ,τ,U,F,A,d,ρ,J definitions are literal.

F defaults to0 at U=∞; the actual law uses the restriction 0<U≤T first. No conditioning normalization, guaranteed finite wait or strict hazard increase is imposed. Zero normal reflection is the identity; flat hazard, T=0 and rank0 are allowed.

Tests are all Borel real h on nonnegative time×full phase, with every M≥0 satisfying a global absolute bound. The three displayed L¹ facts are conclusions. M=0 is included. No unbounded expectation or oracle-cost transfer follows.
